title: 📘 UNIT 7: AFRICA SINCE THE 1960s
notes: 1960s → rapid African decolonization and emergence of independent states.

title: 7.1 🌍 The Road to Independence and the Rise of Independent States in Africa
notes:
African independence movements developed through both peaceful and armed struggles.

Major factors:
• Growth of African nationalism.
• Weakening of European colonial powers after WWII.
• Formation of political parties and nationalist movements.
• Influence of educated African elites.
• Support for self-determination.
• Impact of Pan-Africanism.

📌 The 1960s became known as a major period of African independence.

title: 7.1.1 🇬🇭 Independence of Ghana
notes:
Gold Coast → British colony.

Kwame Nkrumah → leading nationalist figure.

1949 → Convention People's Party (CPP) established.

1957 → Ghana became independent.

📌 Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to achieve independence in the post-WWII period.

title: 7.1.2 🇳🇬 Nigeria and West African Independence
notes:
Nnamdi Azikiwe → important Nigerian nationalist leader.

Nigeria → gained independence from Britain in 1960.

French West Africa → many territories achieved independence relatively peacefully.

Examples:
• Guinea → 1958.
• Senegal → 1960.
• Côte d'Ivoire → 1960.
• Mali → 1960.

📌 West African nationalism was strengthened by organized political movements.

title: 7.1.3 🇩🇿 Algerian War of Independence
notes:
Algeria → French colony with a large European settler population.

1954 → Algerian War of Independence began.

FLN → National Liberation Front led the armed struggle.

1962 → Algeria gained independence from France.

📌 The Algerian struggle was one of the longest and most violent anti-colonial wars in Africa.

title: 7.1.4 🌍 Decolonization of Africa
notes:
Major independence waves:
• 1950s → Ghana, Sudan, Guinea and others.
• 1960s → large-scale independence across Africa.
• 1970s–1980s → remaining Portuguese colonies and other territories gained independence.
• 1990 → Namibia became independent.
• 1994 → apartheid ended and democratic South Africa emerged.

📌 Colonial rule largely disappeared from Africa by the end of the 20th century.

title: 7.2 🏛️ Politics in Independent African States
notes:
Post-independence African states faced major political challenges.

Common developments:
• One-party systems.
• Military coups.
• Personal dictatorships.
• Civil wars.
• Ethnic and regional conflicts.
• Border disputes.
• Neocolonial influence.

📌 Many new governments struggled to build stable democratic institutions.

title: 7.2.1 🎖️ Military Rule
notes:
Military coups became common in several African countries during the 1960s and 1970s.

Examples:
• Ghana.
• Nigeria.
• Togo.
• Uganda.
• Central African Republic.

Causes:
• Political instability.
• Economic problems.
• Weak institutions.
• Corruption.
• Ethnic and regional tensions.
• Conflict between political groups.

title: 7.2.2 👑 Personal Dictatorships
notes:
Some African leaders concentrated political power in themselves.

Examples include:
• Idi Amin → Uganda.
• Jean-Bédel Bokassa → Central African Republic.
• Mobutu Sese Seko → Zaire.
• Francisco Macías Nguema → Equatorial Guinea.

Common features:
• Suppression of opposition.
• Political repression.
• Personality cults.
• Control of state institutions.

title: 7.2.3 🔗 Neocolonialism
notes:
Neocolonialism → indirect domination or influence of powerful foreign countries over formally independent states.

Methods may include:
• Economic dependence.
• Foreign investment and control.
• Unequal trade relations.
• Political influence.
• Military assistance.
• Dependence on foreign technology and aid.

📌 Political independence did not always mean complete economic independence.

title: 7.3 💰 Economy and Society in Independent Africa
notes:
Post-independence African economies inherited colonial economic structures.

Major characteristics:
• Dependence on agricultural exports.
• Dependence on a few primary commodities.
• Limited industrialization.
• Foreign trade dependence.
• Poverty and unemployment.
• Rapid population growth.
• Urbanization.
• Unequal development.

title: 7.3.1 🌾 Agriculture and Natural Resources
notes:
Agriculture remained the main economic activity in many African countries.

Major exports → coffee, cocoa, cotton, tea, tobacco, minerals and petroleum.

Problems:
• Low productivity.
• Dependence on rainfall.
• Drought and famine.
• Poor infrastructure.
• Fluctuating world prices.
• Limited access to modern technology.

title: 7.3.2 🏭 Industrialization and Development
notes:
African governments attempted to promote industrialization through:
• State-owned industries.
• Development planning.
• Infrastructure projects.
• Foreign investment.
• Regional economic cooperation.

Major obstacles:
• Limited capital.
• Weak infrastructure.
• Shortage of skilled labor.
• Small domestic markets.
• Foreign economic dependence.

title: 7.3.3 👥 Population and Social Issues
notes:
Major social challenges:
• Rapid population growth.
• Poverty.
• Unemployment.
• Low literacy in many areas.
• Limited healthcare.
• Urbanization.
• Food insecurity.
• Refugees and internally displaced people.

📌 Governments expanded education and health services, but development remained uneven.

title: 7.4 ❄️ The Cold War and Africa
notes:
The Cold War affected African politics, wars and foreign relations.

USA and USSR competed for influence through:
• Military assistance.
• Economic aid.
• Political support.
• Arms supplies.
• Support for allied governments and movements.

📌 African conflicts often became connected to wider Cold War rivalry.

title: 7.4.1 ⚔️ Cold War Conflicts in Africa
notes:
Major conflicts influenced by Cold War rivalry included:
• Congo Crisis.
• Angolan Civil War.
• Ethiopian–Somali conflict.
• Mozambique conflict.
• Conflicts in southern Africa.

📌 Both superpowers and their allies supported opposing African political and military forces.

title: 7.4.2 🇨🇩 Congo Crisis
notes:
1960 → Congo gained independence from Belgium.

Patrice Lumumba → first Prime Minister.

Congo Crisis → political instability, secession and foreign intervention followed independence.

Lumumba was removed and later killed.

Mobutu Sese Seko eventually established a long-lasting authoritarian regime.

📌 The crisis became an important Cold War confrontation in Africa.

title: 7.4.3 🇦🇴 Angola
notes:
1975 → Angola gained independence from Portugal.

Major groups:
• MPLA.
• UNITA.
• FNLA.

The civil war became internationalized through foreign support.

📌 USSR and Cuba supported MPLA, while UNITA received support from anti-communist powers.

title: 7.4.4 🌍 Southern Africa and Apartheid
notes:
Apartheid → system of racial segregation and white minority rule in South Africa.

Major features:
• Racial classification.
• Separate residential areas.
• Political exclusion of the black majority.
• Restrictions on movement and employment.

ANC → African National Congress led the struggle against apartheid.

Nelson Mandela → major anti-apartheid leader.

1994 → democratic elections ended apartheid-era political rule.

title: 7.5 🤝 Pan-Africanism, OAU and AU
notes:
Pan-Africanism → movement promoting African unity, solidarity, liberation and cooperation.

Major aims:
• End colonialism.
• Oppose racism and apartheid.
• Promote African unity.
• Support political independence.
• Encourage economic cooperation.

📌 Pan-Africanism contributed to African liberation and continental integration.

title: 7.5.1 🌍 Organization of African Unity (OAU)
notes:
OAU → established in Addis Ababa on 25 May 1963.

Major aims:
• Promote African unity and solidarity.
• Defend sovereignty and territorial integrity.
• Coordinate cooperation among African states.
• Eliminate colonialism and apartheid.
• Support liberation movements.
• Promote peace and security.

📌 Ethiopia played an important role in the establishment of the OAU.

title: 7.5.2 🌐 From OAU to African Union
notes:
African Union (AU) → established in 2002, replacing the OAU.

Main goals:
• Greater African integration.
• Peace and security.
• Economic and political cooperation.
• Sustainable development.
• Protection of human rights.
• Promotion of democracy and good governance.

📌 AU institutions include the Assembly, Executive Council, AU Commission and Peace and Security Council.

title: 7.5.3 🕊️ African Peace and Security
notes:
African Peace and Security Architecture (APSA) → framework for preventing and managing conflicts in Africa.

Important components:
• AU Peace and Security Council.
• African Standby Force.
• Continental Early Warning System.
• Panel of the Wise.
• Peace Fund.

📌 The AU increasingly takes responsibility for African peacekeeping and conflict management.

title: 7.6 🌍 Issues in Contemporary Africa
notes:
Major contemporary challenges:
• Poverty and inequality.
• Conflict and insecurity.
• Political instability.
• Terrorism.
• Refugees and displacement.
• Environmental degradation.
• Climate change.
• Food insecurity.
• Rapid population growth.
• Public health challenges.
• Unemployment and underdevelopment.

title: 7.6.1 🌱 Environmental Challenges
notes:
Major environmental problems:
• Deforestation.
• Desertification.
• Soil erosion.
• Drought.
• Water scarcity.
• Loss of biodiversity.
• Climate change.
• Pollution.

Effects → reduced agricultural productivity, food insecurity, displacement and pressure on natural resources.

title: 7.6.2 🕊️ Peace, Security and Conflict
notes:
African peace and security challenges include:
• Civil wars.
• Border disputes.
• Ethnic and political conflicts.
• Terrorism and extremism.
• Political instability.
• Organized crime.

Responses:
• AU peacekeeping.
• Regional organizations.
• Mediation and negotiation.
• UN peacekeeping.
• Conflict prevention and early warning systems.

title: 7.6.3 📈 Development and African Integration
notes:
African development strategies emphasize:
• Regional integration.
• Intra-African trade.
• Infrastructure development.
• Industrialization.
• Education and health.
• Good governance.
• Sustainable use of resources.
• Continental cooperation.

📌 Regional integration aims to strengthen African economies and reduce dependence on external powers.

notes:
